page: Microsoft Azure E48as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is driven by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz, providing 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores via multithreading. It provides an x86_64 architecture equipped with 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster. The instance features a memory capacity of 384.0 GB RAM, delivering a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources include 825 GB of bundled local SSD storage, while discrete GPU acceleration is absent.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid performance in multi-threaded compute and memory operations. The instance achieved top-quartile performance in multi-core evaluations, including stress-ng multi-core testing (64,919.46), Geekbench multi-core scoring (15,937.0), and PassMark CPU overall scoring (51,680.81). Cryptographic workloads perform well due to hardware acceleration extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, reflected by a top-tier PassMark encryption result of 51,516.84. Memory evaluations align with its memory-optimized classification, yielding a high PassMark memory score of 2,969.9. Conversely, the processor lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions, and text generation benchmarks on larger 70B parameter language models remain limited at 2.66 tokens per second.

The 8.0 GB RAM allocation per vCPU makes this configuration resource-dense for memory-intensive architectures without requiring specialized accelerator hardware. Bundled local SSD storage provides quick transient scratch space for operational tasks. Microsoft Azure E48as_v4 is appropriate for large-scale relational databases, distributed caching layers such as Redis clusters, enterprise resource planning platforms, and big data ETL processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E48as_v4 is a memory-optimized cloud virtual machine featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from a 24-core AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. Configured with a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance provides 384.0 GB of system memory, alongside 825 GB of bundled local SSD temporary storage and no discrete GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate strong multi-threaded compute throughput, excellent cryptographic processing with hardware AES and SHA support, and high memory subsystem marks. While lacking AVX-512 vector extensions and exhibiting constrained execution speeds on large-parameter language models, the hardware delivers strong parallel CPU and RAM density. These attributes make it suited for large-scale enterprise databases, memory-resident analytics, distributed caching tiers, and multi-threaded data transformation jobs requiring substantial memory footprints.
